questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the italicised word.

She tried to conceal her bruises with skin-coloured foundation.
questions.solution:
Conceal- withdraw or remove from observation; cover or keep from sight

Reveal- to make known; disclose; to lay open to view; display

So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Diminish- to make or cause to seem smaller, less

questions.question: In the passage, the word "apprenticeship" most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions :Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

The scent of our guild hall was a mix of aging parchment, walnut ink, and the sharp tang of binding glue. For months, my apprenticeship to Master Elara had consisted of the mundane: grinding pigments, stretching vellum, and endless practice of the Rose of the Winds. My hands, stained with a permanent map of blue and ochre inks, ached for a real chart. Then, one rain-swept afternoon, Elara unrolled the Imago Mundi. It was a vast, ancient thing, its edges frayed like a forgotten coastline. The parchment was brittle, the seas a faded aquamarine, and the landmasses were shapes I had never seen in any modern atlas. My task, Elara explained in her hushed, reverent voice, was not merely to copy it, but to renew it. I was to trace every line, re-ink every letter, and breathe life back into its faded splendor. For days, I worked with a devotion bordering on worship. My quill, a feather from a sea eagle, followed the ghost of the original cartographer's hand. I traced jagged mountain ranges that seemed to breathe cold air onto my fingers and deserts so vast they made me thirsty. It was while I was inking a small, unnamed archipelago in the far western sea that the first strange thing happened. I had added a tiny spring to the largest island, a flourish of my own born of a whim, marking it with a droplet of cerulean blue. The next morning, when I returned to my work, a small, damp patch had bloomed on the vellum, precisely where I had drawn the spring. It smelled of fresh rain. Dismissing it as a spilled water pot, I continued. Later, while tracing the edges of the Great Northern Forest, I grew frustrated with a particularly gnarled section. On impulse, I drew a new, clearer path through the dense woods, a clean line of burnt umber. The ink had barely dried when a tremor ran through the stone floor of the guild hall. Master Elara rushed in, her face pale. "A path has opened," she whispered, her eyes wide with a fear I did not understand. "The traders are saying a clear road has appeared overnight in the Great Forest, where none was before." My blood ran cold. I stared at the map, at the lines I had drawn. They were not just ink on parchment. They were cause and effect, a living document of creation. My hand trembled as I looked at the vast, empty spaces on the ancient chart - the Terra Incognita. What would happen if I drew a new mountain? A new river? A new city? The world, I realized, was not a fixed and finished thing to be recorded, but a draft waiting for an author. And in my hand, I held the quill.

options.label: A
options.text: A period of formal education in theory

options.label: B
options.text: A phase of learning under guidance and training

options.label: C
options.text: A stage of independent professional work

options.label: D
options.text: A ceremonial initiation into a guild

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option b).

An apprenticeship is a system where a person, the apprentice, works for a skilled employer or master for a fixed period to learn a particular craft or trade.

The passage clearly illustrates this relationship: The narrator is the apprentice. "Master Elara" is the skilled expert providing guidance. The work described ("grinding pigments, stretching vellum") is the practical, on-the-job training.

This situation perfectly matches the definition in option (b).

a) is incorrect because the tasks described are practical and hands-on, not purely theoretical.

c) is incorrect because an apprenticeship is a stage of learning, before one becomes an independent professional.

d) is incorrect because an initiation is a single ceremony, whereas the passage describes the apprenticeship as a period lasting "for months."

questions.question: Choose the appropriate antonym of the word: Impervious
questions.solution:
Impervious - not allowing fluid to pass through.

Permeable - (of a material or membrane) allowing liquids or gases to pass through it.

So, both words are opposite in meaning to each other.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Descriptive - serving or seeking to describe.

Substantial - of considerable importance, size, or worth.

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 16-18
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The judge dismissed the submission of the extraneous evidence as it was not ____ to the trial.
questions.solution:
The correct choice is (b) pertinent.

· Pertinent: pertaining or relating directly and significantly to the matter at hand; relevant.

· Among the given options, 'pertinent' fits the best in the sentence. The sentence conveys that the judge had dismissed the submission of the evidence as it was not applicable or was not related to the subject matter at hand.

· 'Catered' [verb] and 'Synonyms' [noun] are eliminated as an adjective is required to describe the nature of evidence. 'Gratify' has a different meaning which is inapt in the context of the given sentence.

· Catered: To provide or supply what amuses or is desired; Gratify: to satisfy, indulge, humour, as one's desires or appetites; Synonymous: Equivalent in meaning.

questions.question: The word "inflatable" most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

River rafting is an exhilarating outdoor activity that combines adventure, teamwork, and a deep engagement with nature. It involves navigating a river's currents using an (5) inflatable raft, often through stretches of turbulent water known as rapids. These rapids are classified on a scale that indicates their difficulty, ranging from gentle flows suitable for beginners to intense, fast-moving sections that demand skill and experience. Participants must work in _(1)_ , following the guide's instructions to paddle in rhythm and maintain balance, as even a slight miscalculation can disrupt the raft's stability. Beyond the thrill, river rafting offers a unique opportunity to _(2)_with the natural environment, as rafters are surrounded by scenic landscapes such as forests, cliffs, and open skies. It also fosters qualities such as trust, communication, and resilience, as each member plays a vital role in navigating the challenges of the river.

However, the activity requires careful attention to safety, and proper gear is _(3)_ to ensure protection against potential risks. In recent years, river rafting has gained popularity as both a (4) recreational pursuit and a form of eco-tourism. When practised responsibly, it encourages appreciation for rivers while promoting sustainable travel practices that help preserve natural ecosystems.

options.label: A
options.text: Capable of being filled with air

questions.solution: Among the given options, (a) Capable of being filled with air is the best fit because "inflatable" refers to an object that can be expanded or made firm by filling it with air or gas, as in the case of a raft. Hence, (a) Capable of being filled with air is the correct answer. Made of solid material suggests rigidity, difficult to carry refers to weight or portability, and used only in emergencies limits the usage context, none of which convey the meaning of "inflatable."

questions.question: Which of the following is a homonym of plait?
questions.solution:
Among the given options, Plat is the correct answer because PLAIT and PLAT are pronounced alike (/plæt/) but have different meanings. A plait is a braid or an arrangement of intertwined strands, while a plat is a map or plan of a piece of land. Therefore, they form a homophone pair.

Option (a) Plate is incorrect because plate is pronounced /pleɪt/, which differs from the pronunciation of plait.

Option (c) Pleat is incorrect because pleat is pronounced /pliːt/ and refers to a fold in fabric.

Option (d) Plight is incorrect because plight is pronounced /plaɪt/ and means a difficult or unfortunate situation.

Hence, Option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

There has been widespread speculation that he plans to quit his position.
questions.solution:
'Speculation' means the process of thinking. 'Contemplation' means being highly concentrated in thought. So, the two words can be used as synonyms of each other. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

'Abstention' means the act of restraining oneself.

'Disregard' means the act of deliberately not paying attention.

'Medication' means the administration of medicine.

questions.question:

We are looking for a person who provides expert advice professionally for our crisis.
questions.solution:
Rescuer- a person who saves someone from a dangerous or difficult situation.

Consultant- a person who provides expert advice professionally.

Analyst- a person who analyses or who is skilled in analysis.

Expert- a person who is very knowledgeable about or skilful in a particular area.

Among the given options, the word that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined phrase is option (b), 'consultant'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question: In the passage, the word "infrequently" most nearly means
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

Many people use the expression "once in a blue moon" to describe an event that happens very rarely. Because the phrase is so common, some assume that a blue moon is purely imaginary. In reality, however, a blue moon is an actual astronomical phenomenon, though it does not usually refer to a moon that appears blue in colour.

The most widely accepted definition of a blue moon is the occurrence of a second full moon within a single calendar month. Since the lunar cycle lasts about 29.5 days, most months contain only one full moon. Occasionally, however, the timing allows two full moons to occur in the same month. This unusual event happens approximately once every two or three years, making it relatively rare but far from impossible.

Historically, the term "blue moon" has also been used in another way. Some calendars defined it as the third full moon in a season containing four full moons instead of the usual three. Although astronomers recognise both definitions, the monthly definition is more widely known today. On very rare occasions, atmospheric conditions such as volcanic eruptions or large forest fires can even cause the moon to appear slightly bluish, though this is not the reason behind the term.

The rarity of the phenomenon eventually inspired the idiom "once in a blue moon." Over time, the expression came to signify something that occurs infrequently. Thus, a phrase that many regard as figurative actually has its origins in a genuine astronomical event.
questions.solution:
Among the given options, (d) on rare occasions is the correct answer because the passage explains that the idiom "once in a blue moon" refers to something that happens very rarely. In this context, "infrequently" means not often or only on rare occasions. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is incorrect because it refers to consistency rather than rarity.

Option (b) is incorrect because a fixed interval implies regular occurrence.

Option (c) is incorrect because it is opposite in meaning to "infrequently."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.

The ___ of friends giggled together, forming a tight circle in the school hallway.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank is 'clique'. "Clique" refers to a small, exclusive group of people who associate closely and often exclude others. In the given sentence, it suggests that a group of friends giggled together, forming a tight circle in the school hallway. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence. "Cluck" typically refers to the sound made by a chicken. "Cleek" refers to a hook-shaped instrument. "Click" refers to a short, sharp sound or operating a computer mouse.

The complete sentence is: The clique of friends giggled together, forming a tight circle in the school hallway.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Pick the spelling that is correct for a short interesting story about a real person or event.
questions.solution: Among the given options, anecdote is the correct spelling referring to a brief and often amusing account of a real incident or person. The other options contain spelling errors: anacdote replaces the vowel "e" with "a", anecdout changes the final vowel pattern, and anecdoat introduces an incorrect vowel sequence. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Main streets are where communities unite to celebrate, where cultures are exchanged, and where writers and pollsters stroll, ____________ to take the nation's pulse.
questions.solution: Plague - causes distress to someone. Eager - enthusiastic. Vigour - physical strength and good health. Meagre - lacking in quality or quantity. We need an adjective here to describe "writers and pollsters", so a) and c) are incorrect, as a) is a verb/noun and c) is a noun. Between the remaining options, b) is the right answer as it gives the meaning that they show enthusiasm. 'Meagre' does not make the sentence meaningful. Hence, option b) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Trenchant
questions.solution:
Trenchant: Vigorous or incisive in expression or style; clearly or sharply defined.

Astute: Having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage; sagacious.

The other options - Pacific (peaceful), Benevolent (kind), and Timid (lacking courage) are antonyms or unrelated in meaning.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Which spelling is correct for taking offense or annoyance?
questions.solution:
"Umbrage" means "a feeling of offense, annoyance, or resentment".

Usage: She took umbrage at his sarcastic remark during the meeting.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A strong verbal or written attack on someone or something.
questions.solution:
Polemic: A strong and often aggressive written or spoken attack on a particular opinion, belief, or person.

Eulogy: A speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, typically someone who has just died.

Critique: A detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

Exhortation: An address or communication emphatically urging someone to do something.

So, "a strong verbal or written attack" is a "polemic".

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

An albatross around one's neck

options.label: C
options.text: A persistent and burdensome problem or source of guilt

options.label: D
options.text: To be protected by a powerful entity

questions.solution:
This idiom refers to a heavy burden of guilt or a persistent problem that is a constant reminder of a past mistake.

For example: "The massive debt from his failed business became an albatross around his neck for years."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.

options.label: A
options.text: Most of the studies in this field focus on individual species of animal or plant.

options.label: B
options.text: He discovered an ancient coin while digging in his backyard.

options.label: C
options.text: Antimicrobial resistance leads to more deaths and ilness in Africa compared to anywhere else.

questions.solution:
All the sentences have correct spelling except for the one mentioned in option (c).

questions.question: Which of the following is a homonym of mote?
questions.solution:
Option (c) is correct because MOAT is pronounced like MOTE but has a different meaning. A mote is a tiny particle, especially of dust, while a moat is a deep ditch around a fort or castle. The rule is that such words are identified through matching sound, not similar spelling.

• Option (a) is incorrect because MUTE has a different vowel sound.

• Option (b) is incorrect because MOOT is pronounced differently.

• Option (d) is incorrect because MATE does not match the pronunciation of MOTE.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words/phrases.

A person who is extremely enthusiastic.
questions.solution:
'Fanatic' means a person who is extremely enthusiastic. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Fatalist: A person who believes that all events are predetermined and inevitable.

Sedative: A substance that induces sedation by reducing irritability or excitement.

Sceptic: A person inclined to question or doubt accepted opinions.

questions.question: What is the synonym of "Obdurate"?
questions.solution: Obdurate means "stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action." The closest meaning should therefore indicate firmness or stubborn resistance. Intransigent means "unwilling to change one's views or agree about something," which closely matches the meaning of obdurate. The other options do not express this meaning: compliant means willing to follow rules or requests, amenable means open to suggestion or persuasion, and malleable means easily influenced or shaped. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Obstinate
questions.solution:
"Obstinate" means unreasonably stubborn, unwilling to change one's opinion or behavior, even when persuaded.

Stubborn - Synonym, not an antonym.

Flexible - Correct. Willing to change or adapt; opposite of obstinate.

Inflexible - Synonym; similar in meaning to obstinate.

Recalcitrant - Also means stubborn or resistant to authority; synonym.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word "amplified" :
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

In the digital age, social media has become a powerful force in shaping what people see, think, and discuss. With platforms under Meta Platforms increasingly interconnected, the boundaries between different apps have blurred significantly. Content that appears on Instagram is often repurposed and circulated on YouTube Shorts, Facebook, and Threads. As a result, users across platforms are frequently exposed to the same videos, trends, and narratives, creating a sense that everyone is consuming identical content regardless of where they scroll. This interconnected ecosystem has made content highly transferable, reducing diversity in what people encounter online.

This uniformity of content has deeper implications than mere repetition. When millions of users engage with the same posts, ideas gain rapid visibility and acceptance, often without critical evaluation. In such an environment, fake news or misleading information can spread like wildfire. A single piece of unverified content, once amplified across multiple platforms, begins to appear credible simply due to its widespread presence. Similarly, negative propaganda directed towards an individual or institution can quickly turn into what seems like a unanimous public opinion. The repetition of the same narrative across different apps creates an illusion of truth, making it difficult for users to distinguish between fact and manipulation.

Moreover, algorithms play a crucial role in reinforcing this cycle by promoting content that generates high engagement, often prioritising sensationalism over accuracy. This leads to echo chambers where users repeatedly encounter the same viewpoints, further strengthening their beliefs without exposure to alternative perspectives. Therefore, in an era where content is interconnected and rapidly disseminated, it becomes essential for individuals to be mindful of their digital consumption. One must question the authenticity of what they watch, verify information before accepting it, and avoid blindly sharing content. Responsible consumption is no longer a choice but a necessity, as the information we engage with has the power to shape opinions, influence behaviour, and impact society at large.
questions.solution: Among the given options, (b) Spread is the best fit because "amplified" in the context of the passage refers to content being increased in reach and visibility across platforms. This usage appears in paragraph 2. Hence, (b) is the correct answer. Option (a) is the opposite in meaning, while (c) and (d) do not fit the context.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence:

The documentary filmmaker was known for her ________ approach, presenting both sides of controversial social issues without expressing personal judgment.
questions.question_hi:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence:

The documentary filmmaker was known for her ________ approach, presenting both sides of controversial social issues without expressing personal judgment.
questions.solution:
✅ Correct Answer: impartial (निष्पक्ष / पक्षपात रहित)

Explanation:

Sentence: The documentary filmmaker was known for her ________ approach, presenting both sides of controversial social issues without expressing personal judgment.

  • The word that best fits is impartial, meaning fair, unbiased, and neutral.
  • Other options do not fit the context of balanced presentation.

Why Other Options Are Wrong:

  • partisan (पक्षपाती / दलगत) → ❌ Shows bias toward one side, opposite of the intended meaning.
  • whimsical (मनमौजी / सनकी) → ❌ Means unpredictable or fanciful, not suitable for serious documentary work.
  • vitriolic (कटु / तीखा) → ❌ Means bitter or harsh criticism, opposite of neutral tone.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Jump the shark

options.label: A
options.text: To take a dangerous and life-threatening risk

options.label: B
options.text: The point at which something, once popular, declines into absurdity

options.label: C
options.text: To achieve sudden and unexpected success

options.label: D
options.text: To switch one's loyalty or allegiance at a critical time

questions.solution:
This is a modern idiom used to describe the moment when a creative work (like a long-running television show) begins a decline in quality, often marked by a particularly ridiculous plot twist intended to maintain viewers' interest.

For example: "Many fans felt the series jumped the shark when the main characters were abducted by aliens."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses the idiom correctly.

options.label: A
options.text: He was feeling very cold shoulder even during a hot day.

options.label: B
options.text: My cold shoulder does not allow me to move my hand any further.

options.label: C
options.text: I got the cold shoulder from Anna at the party.

options.label: D
options.text: My shoulder got cold in the winters.

questions.solution:
'Cold shoulder' means to deliberately ignore someone. The use of the idiom is correctly mentioned in the statement of option (c). It suggests that the subject was feeling ignored.

Hence, option (c) is correct.
